key_insight: RSI-Anything shows how an AI system can use predictive world models to turn experience into lasting improvements, while deciding when those models need to be updated. The key idea is to make recursive self-improvement more practical by balancing prediction, learning-data selection, and safeguards against model drift.
problem_solved: The paper addresses two core RSI challenges: external feedback is expensive to collect, and world-model predictions can become unreliable as the policy or system changes over time.
method: Builds on JEPA-Anything with a domain-general framework that uses predictive world models to guide both action selection and learning-data selection.
Uses observed feedback to improve the policy or workflow, while also triggering conditional adaptation of the world model when needed.
Adds component checks and compatibility checks to reduce errors when system parts evolve or interact in unexpected ways.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical template for building self-improving systems that learn efficiently from experience without relying heavily on costly feedback. It is especially relevant for agents, automated workflows, and adaptive systems that must stay reliable as they evolve.

paper_title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
paper_authors: Taoyong Cui, Pinxian Zeng, Wanghan Xu, Hao Xiao, Shuhan Xue
